entities.name: Zenobius of Florence
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Zenobius of Florence (337–417 CE) was the first bishop of Florence and a revered figure in the Catholic Church. As a key figure in early Christian history, he played a significant role in shaping the spiritual landscape of the city.

 Born into a wealthy family, Zenobius was educated in Rome and later became a monk before being ordained as a priest. His leadership skills and commitment to his faith earned him the respect of his peers, and he was eventually appointed as the bishop of Florence by Emperor Honorius in 402 CE.

 During his tenure as bishop, Zenobius oversaw the construction of several churches and monasteries, including the iconic Basilica di San Miniato al Monte. He also worked to establish trade relationships with neighboring cities and promote the growth of agriculture in the region.

 Zenobius' legacy extends beyond his religious contributions. As a patron of the arts, he supported local artists and writers, fostering a vibrant cultural scene in Florence.

 The feast day of Saint Zenobius is celebrated on May 25, and his tomb has been venerated as a shrine since the 5th century CE.
